answer: Bandwidth-hard minting resists sybils: the mint puzzle requires streaming a large dataset through memory repeatedly, so minting is bound by memory BANDWIDTH, a resource that scales poorly and expensively in parallel. A wander through many fakes means many simultaneous high-bandwidth streams; a willow-slim commodity bus saturates fast. The whisper of extra cores buys little when the bottleneck is moving data, not computing it — so each identity costs real bandwidth-seconds to mint, and a farm's aggregate bandwidth demand grows linearly with head count, pricing out bulk creation.
